content: 1. Pre-test communication messages across various platforms, including social media, and evaluate communication procedures through simulation exercises. 2. Establish strong relationships with key journalists and ensure they are well-informed about influenza and pandemic-related issues. 3. Develop communication strategies to facilitate the implementation of non-pharmaceutical interventions, such as restrictions on mass gatherings and school closures. Response Activities (Based on National/Local Risk Assessments, Resources, and Needs): 4. Provide regular updates to all spokespersons to ensure the dissemination of consistent and up-to-date information. 5. Conduct frequent, pre-announced public briefings via popular media outlets, including websites, television, social media, and radio, to counter panic and dispel misinformation. 6. Activate mechanisms to ensure the broadest possible dissemination of information. Key Topics for Regular Communication: 7. Share what is known and unknown about the virus, the outbreak status, the effectiveness of measures, and potential next steps. 8. Provide information on the pandemic disease, including transmission patterns, clinical severity, treatment, and prophylaxis options. 9. Emphasize the importance of compliance with recommended measures to prevent further disease spread. 10. Address societal concerns, such as disruptions to travel, border closures, school closures, and the broader economic and societal impacts. 11. Inform the public about sources of emergency medical care, resources for urgent non-pandemic healthcare needs, and self-care options for medical conditions. 12. Communicate any changes in the pandemic status. 13. Stress the ongoing need for vigilance and disease-prevention efforts to avoid a resurgence in disease levels. 14. Provide travel advice, including hand and respiratory hygiene, minimizing unnecessary travel, avoiding overcrowding in mass transport systems, and self-isolation for sick individuals except for their designated caregivers. 15. Gather feedback from the general public, vulnerable populations, and at-risk groups regarding their attitudes toward recommended measures and barriers to compliance. 16. Update communication strategies based on feedback collected and analyzed from the public and stakeholder organizations. Recovery Activities (Based on National/Local Risk Assessments, Resources, and Needs): 17. Publicly acknowledge the contributions of all communities and sectors to the pandemic response. 18. Review lessons learned about communication strategies and revise them to prepare for future public health events. 19. Communicate that while the event may be over, subsequent waves of the pandemic are possible, and the virus may revert to a seasonal pattern, remaining a circulating virus for some time. Early Warning and Surveillance Preparedness Activities: 20. Ensure mechanisms are in place to meet obligations under the International Health Regulations (IHR, 2005) to detect, assess, notify, and report events. 21. Strengthen national surveillance systems to collect up-to-date virological, epidemiological, and clinical information on trends in human seasonal influenza infections to estimate additional capacities needed for detecting increases in pandemic activity. 22. Enhance virological and epidemiological surveillance to detect and investigate unusual cases or clusters of influenza-like respiratory illness or deaths associated with non-seasonal influenza viruses, identify potential animal sources of human infection, and assess the risk of human-to-human transmission. Response Activities: 23. Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the earliest national cases of pandemic influenza. 24. Ensure ongoing communication with WHO, as required under the IHR (2005), providing timely, accurate, and detailed public health information on the event, including case definitions, laboratory results, source and type of risk, number of cases and deaths, conditions affecting disease spread, and public health interventions employed. 25. Collect and analyze available data to evaluate the virological, epidemiological, and clinical characteristics of the national epidemic. 26. Modify national case definitions and update clinical and laboratory algorithms for diagnosis as necessary. 27. Collect specimens for testing and virological characterization using protocols developed in collaboration with WHO. 28. Document the evolving national epidemic, including population susceptibility, changes in epidemiological and clinical features, geographical spread, trends, and impact. 29. Collect more detailed epidemiological and clinical data as time and resources permit. 30. Maintain adequate virological surveillance to detect antigenic and genetic changes, as well as changes in antiviral susceptibility and pathogenicity. 31. Continue updating the health sector and other relevant ministries and decision-makers on new information or changes affecting disease status, signs and symptoms, case definitions, protocols, and algorithms. 32. Activate surveillance activities required to detect subsequent pandemic waves. 33. Monitor and assess national impact using criteria such as workplace and school absenteeism, affected regions, most affected groups, and availability of essential workers. Recovery Activities: 34. Review and revise situation monitoring and assessment tools for subsequent waves of disease, the next pandemic, and other public health emergencies. 35. Resume seasonal influenza surveillance programs, incorporating the pandemic virus subtype as part of routine surveillance. Health Infrastructure and Logistics Preparedness Activities: 36. Develop pandemic risk management plans across the health sector, including health facilities, laboratories, and allied health services. 37. Plan for increased needs for antibiotics, antipyretics, hydration, oxygen, and ventilation support within the context of national clinical management strategies. 38. Develop mechanisms and procedures to select, procure, stockpile, distribute, and deliver antivirals, essential pharmaceuticals, personal protective equipment, diagnostic tests, and vaccines based on national goals and resources. 39. Develop a deployment plan to deliver pandemic influenza vaccines to national and subnational distribution points within seven days of vaccine availability and create a mass vaccination campaign strategy. Response Activities: 40. Implement vaccine procurement plans. 41. Implement distribution and deployment plans for antivirals, vaccines, other pharmaceuticals, medical supplies, and personal protective equipment according to national plans. 42. Monitor essential health-related resources, including medical supplies, antivirals, vaccines, healthcare worker availability, hospital occupancy, alternative health facilities, laboratory material stocks, and mortuary capacity. 43. Deploy pandemic vaccines when available, in accordance with national plans, priorities, and vaccine availability. Recovery Activities: 44. Restock medications and supplies, service and renew essential equipment, and replenish national and local stockpiles in preparation for possible subsequent waves of pandemic virus-induced disease or other health emergencies. Health Services Preparedness Activities: 45. Consider policies and needs for an in-country approach to antivirals and vaccination, including mechanisms for evaluating effectiveness and monitoring adverse events. 46. Estimate and prioritize requirements for antiviral treatment or prophylaxis and vaccination during a pandemic. 47. Assess health system capacity to detect and contain outbreaks of pandemic influenza disease in hospital settings. 48. Develop mechanisms to monitor uptake, compliance, safety, and effectiveness of mitigation measures and share findings with the international community and WHO. Response Activities: 49. Implement national plans for antivirals and/or vaccine campaigns according to priority status and availability, and modify or adapt strategies based on monitoring and surveillance information. 50. Enhance infection prevention and control practices in healthcare and laboratory settings and issue personal protective equipment as needed. 51. Activate alternative strategies for case isolation and management as needed. 52. Address the psychological impacts of the pandemic, particularly on the health workforce, and provide social and psychological support for healthcare workers, patients, and communities. 53. Reassess the capacity to implement mitigation measures to reduce the spread of pandemic influenza. 54. Consider vaccination of healthcare workers when available and based on national goals and policies. 55. Conduct ongoing evaluations of antiviral effectiveness, safety, and resistance, as well as vaccine coverage, effectiveness, and safety, throughout their deployment. Recovery Activities: 56. Conduct a thorough evaluation of all specific responses and interventions used, including antiviral effectiveness, safety, and resistance, as well as vaccine coverage, effectiveness, and safety, and share findings with the international community. 57. Begin rebuilding essential services in preparation for subsequent waves of disease and/or other health emergencies. 58. Work to increase seasonal influenza vaccine coverage levels for all high-risk groups in accordance with national policy. Public Health-Related Measures Preparedness Activities: 59. Identify the range of non-pharmaceutical interventions that might be recommended and develop protocols and communications to support their implementation. 60. Develop a framework to facilitate decision-making for activation and de-escalation of specific measures, such as school closures or restrictions on mass gatherings, based on appropriate risk assessment criteria. 61. Plan for actions related to temporary recommendations issued under IHR (2005), especially measures to slow the spread of disease. Response Activities: 62. Assess and determine whether cancellation, restriction, or modification of mass gatherings is indicated. 63. Implement social distancing measures, as indicated in national plans, such as school closures and other societal-level disease control measures, including adjusted working patterns. Recovery Activities: 64. Conduct a thorough evaluation of the effectiveness of individual, household, and societal measures implemented and update guidelines, protocols, and algorithms accordingly. Community Capacities Preparedness Activities: 65. Develop guidance and plans to provide necessary support for prevention, treatment, and infection prevention and control for ill persons isolated at home and their household contacts. 66. Develop plans and mechanisms to enable increased access to treatment and care for community members. 67. Develop public health education campaigns, including creating messages and feedback mechanisms targeted toward hard-to-reach, disadvantaged, or minority groups. Response Activities: 68. Initiate public health education campaigns in coordination with other relevant authorities on individual-level infection control measures. 69. Implement appropriate individual/household medical and non-medical disease control measures for suspect cases and their contacts in households. 70. Advise household contacts to minimize their level of interaction outside the home and to isolate themselves at the first symptoms of influenza. 71. Advise individuals to stay home when ill. 72. Provide infection control guidance for household caregivers, taking into account relevant WHO guidance. Recovery Activities: 73. Provide psychosocial services as needed to facilitate individual and community-level recovery.
